dialog.body: Finance Department, this is Janet Whitcomb. How may I direct your call?
Oh, hi, sorry, I know this is silly, but before I start, is this the right extension for property tax questions? I like to confirm I have the right extension first, otherwise I get bounced around.
Yes, you've reached the correct office. Property tax questions come through Finance. What can I help you with?

Okay, good. Sorry, my name is Anabela Brito. I rent at 191 Narragansett Avenue, in the Fifth Ward. My landlord said the tax bill is something he passes along, sort of, and I got confused about it. I know this is silly, but is there a senior exemption? Or a veteran one? I'm not sure which one applies to somebody like me.
Understood. Exemptions are generally applied to the property owner's bill, ma'am. Are you the owner of record, or is the property owned by your landlord?
Sorry, no, I rent. The landlord owns it. But he said if there was something for seniors I should ask. I'm in my fifties, so, I don't know if that even counts. Sorry.

There are elderly exemptions and veteran exemptions available, and each has its own eligibility requirements. Age and ownership would both matter. Since you're a tenant, you would not apply on your own behalf. The owner would have to apply for any exemption tied to the property.
Oh. Sorry, so I can't apply myself at all? I thought the form was something I fill out and send in.

Not as a renter, no. The application is filed by the property owner with the Tax Assessor's office, and it is generally due by a deadline each year. If you yourself were a veteran, that would not transfer to a property you do not own.
Okay, sorry, I think I get it. Sorry, I know this is silly, but is there a form number? So I can tell him? He's not great with this stuff and I'd rather give him the exact name.

I don't have a form number in front of me that I can state with confidence. The Assessor's office can tell you the exact form for each exemption. I can transfer you, or you may ask your landlord to contact them directly.
Sorry, so it's the Assessor, not Finance? I thought taxes were all the same place.
It's a common mix-up. Finance handles billing and collection. The Assessor determines the valuation and processes exemptions. So the bill comes from us, but the exemption application goes to them.
Okay. Sorry, so he'd call them, and they'd give him the form. And the age thing, does the senior one start at, like, sixty-five? Is that right?
I would not want to state the age requirement incorrectly. The Assessor's office can confirm the criteria. Would you like me to transfer you now?
Sorry, yes please. And, um, if it drops, do I call back this same extension? I'd rather make sure.
If the transfer fails, call the main City Hall line and ask for the Assessor's office. I'll stay on until it connects. One moment, please.
Okay, thank you. Sorry for all the questions.
No trouble at all. Please hold.
Ms. Brito, I'm getting a voicemail at the Assessor's desk. Would you prefer to leave a message there, or try again later this morning?
Sorry, um, I'll try later. So just to repeat, the landlord applies, through the Assessor, not Finance. And I ask them for the form name. Is that right?
That is correct. The owner applies through the Assessor's office, and they can name the form and the requirements.
Okay. Thank you, Ms. Whitcomb. Sorry, I'm still a little mixed up, but I'll try them. Happy holidays.
Happy holidays to you as well. Goodbye.
